paragraphs.text: See 2Ki 18:13, &c. When Hezekiah had set all things in good order, up came Sennacherib with his army. So after sweet communion with God, at the sacrament or otherwise, look for "leviathan, that crooked serpent," to disturb all.
paragraphs.anchor: After these things.

paragraphs.text: Or, And the truth or faithfulness thereof, i.e., of the author in relating them, or rather of Hezekiah in transacting them. Postquam haec fideliter sunt gesta: so Munster rendereth it.
paragraphs.anchor: And the establishment thereof.

paragraphs.text: Heb., To break them up, or to divide them, sow dissension among them, which is the mother of dissolution. Divide et impera. Divide and conquer. His father had carried away, captive the ten tribes: he doubted not, therefore but he should conquer the other two; but his hopes ran aground, as the proverb hath it.
paragraphs.anchor: And thought to win them for himself.

paragraphs.text: See on 2Ki 18:13.
paragraphs.anchor: That Sennacherib was come.

paragraphs.text: He trusted in God: but yet used the best means. God is to be trusted, but not tempted. See Isa 22:9; Isa 22:11.
paragraphs.anchor: To stop the waters of the fountains.

paragraphs.text: Called Gihon. {2Ch 32:30} This was one of those rivers the waters whereof made glad the city of God. See 1Ki 1:33.
paragraphs.anchor: And the brook.

paragraphs.text: Take we like care that Satan, when he cometh to assault us, find not much matter. "Mortify therefore your earthly members, fornication, … and covetousness." {Col 3:5}
paragraphs.anchor: Come and find much water.

paragraphs.text: Or, Mounted the warlike engines upon the towers, for his better defence.
paragraphs.anchor: And raised it up to the towers.

paragraphs.text: He did all that could be done: for he knew that the Assyrian came with a mighty force, as a river that "cometh up over all his channels, and goeth over all his banks." {Isa 8:7}
paragraphs.anchor: He set captains of war.

paragraphs.text: His speech is short but pithy: very cordial and comfortable.
paragraphs.anchor: Be strong and courageous.

paragraphs.text: Only go to Christ and say, as Isa 8:8, "The stretching out of his wings hath filled the breadth of thy land, O Immanuel."
paragraphs.anchor: Now for all the multitude that is with him.

paragraphs.text: Flesh is frail: and God can make the strongest sinew in his arm to crack quickly.
paragraphs.anchor: With him is an arm of flesh.

paragraphs.text: The import of "Immanuel"; by which name Christ now began to be known amongst them.
paragraphs.anchor: But with us is the Lord our God.

paragraphs.text: See 2Ki 18:9. Antichrist, in like sort, sendeth his legates and nuncios to solicit people to a defection from Christ; as he did Vergerius to Saxony, Campeius to the princes of Germany, Sadoletus to Geneva, Pool hither, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: Sent his servants to Jerusalem.

paragraphs.text: Like rhetoric hereunto useth Antichrist, where he would seduce. See Sadolet’s sugared Epistle to the Citizens of Geneva, written in Calvin’s absence, who fully and elegantly answered it from Strasburg, where for a while he lived an exile.
paragraphs.anchor: Whereon do ye trust.

paragraphs.text: Doth not Hezekiah persuade (or deceive) you?] See on 2Ki 18:29-30.

So saith Antichrist, Have not your reformers taken away the abbeys, monasteries, altars, crosses, &c.? And as there wanted not some in Jerusalem who were of the same mind with Sennacherib’s messengers, so neither wanteth there among us a malignant party, that grumble and grind their teeth at our happy Reformation.
paragraphs.anchor: Hath not the same Hezekiah taken away his high places?
Know you not.
That my fathers utterly destroyed.

paragraphs.text: See 2Ki 18:29.
paragraphs.anchor: Now therefore let not Hezekiah.

paragraphs.text: Prodigious blasphemy! And was not that of John Hunt, a a Popish pamphleteer, every whit as bad, when he said, The God of the Protestants is the most uncivil and evil mannered God of all those who have borne the names of gods upon the earth; yea, worse than Pan, god of the clowns, which can endure no ceremonies nor good manners at all! {a}
paragraphs.anchor: How much less shall your God.

paragraphs.text: {a} Humble Appeal to King James, chap. 6.
Adding of their own to their master’s mandates which yet needed not.
paragraphs.anchor: And his servants spake yet more.
He wrote also letters.

To sow the seeds of sedition amongst them, to make division, and thereby get dominion.
paragraphs.anchor: To affright them, and to trouble them.

paragraphs.text: This was high blasphemy. See on 2Ch 32:15 2Ki 17:30; 2Ki 17:33-41.
paragraphs.anchor: As against the gods of the people of the earth.
For this cause.

paragraphs.text: And the prophet Isaiah … prayed.] And at the same time prophesied comfortably. {2Ki 19:14-19}
See 2Ki 19:35.

paragraphs.text: He was not so much preserved, as reserved to a greater mischief
paragraphs.anchor: So he returned with shame of face.
And when he was come.

paragraphs.text: Who were not only preserved, but much enriched by the spoil of their enemies.
paragraphs.anchor: And the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

paragraphs.text: As a careful shepherd doth his flock.
paragraphs.anchor: And guided them on every side.

paragraphs.text: Many strangers were hereupon proselyted, like as Jethro also had been by God’s great works for his people against the Egyptians.
paragraphs.anchor: And many brought gifts unto the Lord.
In those days Hezekiah was sick to the death.

paragraphs.text: His returns were not answerable to his receipts. Plerique omnes sumus ingrati. The rain comes down from heaven in showers; it goes up but in mists: so do our praises return slowly and slenderly. We serve God, for most part as little children serve us, who, when they be come in to us from their play, and have got something of us they want, away they go, without reverence or respect of us; but if they know we will have duty, then they do it, but in such a fashion that we may see their hearts are on their game abroad more than on their duty.
paragraphs.anchor: But Hezekiah rendered not again.

paragraphs.text: Not as good Jehoshaphat’s was, {2Ch 17:6} but worse, with pride and self-conceit, whilst he considered not his distance from God and dependence upon God, but acted as if he had been some petty god within himself. Such a blab Satan will easily blow up in the best hearts, if they watch not.
paragraphs.anchor: For his heart was lifted up.

paragraphs.text: He afflicted himself with voluntary sorrows, when once, by the preaching of the prophet, he came to a sight of his sin. Submissior factus est superbia cordis sui - so Vatablus rendereth it - he was made more humble by the pride of his heart: as God’s people are gainers by their sins also; whence that paradox of Augustine, My sins, in some sense, do me more good than my graces; for they make me afterwards more humble, more careful, more thankful for a Saviour, more merciful to others, more desirous of the state of perfection, &c. See 2Ki 20:17-19.
paragraphs.anchor: Notwithstanding Hezekiah humbled himself.

paragraphs.text: And these puffed him up; his heart was lifted up with his wealth, as a boat riseth with the rising of the water that carrieth it.
paragraphs.anchor: And Hezekiah had exceeding much riches and honour.

paragraphs.text: Heb., Instruments of desire. All these were lawful enough, and useful, had he not shot his affections too far into them.
paragraphs.anchor: And for all manner of pleasant jewels.

paragraphs.text: “ Difficile est amimos opibus non tradere. ”

These are commodities less precious, but more necessary than the former, as the great Caliph of Babylon found when famished to death in the midst of his great treasure, whereof he was willed to eat and make no spare. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: For the increase of corn, wine, and oil.

paragraphs.text: {a} Turk. Hist., fol. 113.
That is, The wealth of this world; though to speak properly, true grace only is "substance, durable substance": riches are nec vera, nec vestra {Luk 16:11-12}
paragraphs.anchor: For God had given him substance very much.

paragraphs.text: See 2Ch 32:4.
paragraphs.anchor: Stopped the upper watercourse of Gihon.

paragraphs.text: See 2Ki 18:7.
paragraphs.anchor: And Hezekiah prospered.
Howbeit in the business of the ambassadors.

paragraphs.text: As he oft doth his best children, {Gen 22:1 Job 1:12; Job 2:3; Job 2:6} but forsaketh them not utterly. {Psa 119:8} The humility that Hezekiah showed when the prophet admonished him, and his perseverance in piety, do show that God never quite deprived him of his grace: only sivit eum agere ex affectu suo, he let him, for this once, do as he would, not strengthening him by his Spirit in this temptation of worldly ambition, that he might discover him to himself and to others; for that a man is, that he is in a temptation. Satan can work but according to the matter he findeth in us. The wind addeth no water to the sea, only can make the waves to rise and surge. The fire addeth nothing to the water when it is set upon it, but attenuateth it only, and causeth it to boil, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: God left him, to try him.

paragraphs.text: Heb., His kindnesses; viz., to God’s people in supplying themwith sacrifices, and setting up the sincere service of God.
paragraphs.anchor: And his goodness.
